newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul core blue chips fall after share limit rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul core blue chips fall after share limit rise.

text.p: South Korea's primary blue chips fell in early Friday trading despite aggressive foreign buying on the first day of a rise in the ceiling on foreign ownership, brokers said.
SK Telecom lost 21,000 won, or 4.8 percent, to 435,000 and POSCO shed 200 won to 53,400.
Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank dropped 500 won each to 13,500 and 10,700.
An official at the Korean Stock Exchange said foreign investors had already snapped up 27 shares in early morning trading including Samsung Electronics, POSCO and SK Telecom.
Samsung Electronics opened weak but had gained 1,200 won to 61,800 at 10:30 am (0130 GMT).
